metadata.title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding

problem.statement: Pre-trained language models are usually computationally expensive, making them difficult to efficiently execute on resource-restricted devices.
limitations_of_prior_work: Pre-trained language models (PLMs) like BERT have a large number of parameters and long inference times, which hinders their deployment on edge devices.
The pre-training-then-fine-tuning paradigm of BERT increases the difficulty of BERT distillation, requiring effective KD strategies for both training stages.

method.name: TinyBERT
method.key_idea: Proposes a novel Transformer distillation method specially designed for knowledge distillation of Transformer-based models and a two-stage learning framework (general distillation and task-specific distillation) to effectively transfer knowledge from a large teacher BERT to a small student TinyBERT at both pre-training and task-specific learning stages.

components.name: Transformer distillation
components.function: A method to distill knowledge from Transformer-based models, including attention-based and hidden states-based distillation, by fitting representations from different layers of the teacher BERT.

components.name: Two-stage learning framework
components.function: Ensures TinyBERT captures both general-domain and task-specific knowledge by performing distillation at both the pre-training (general distillation) and fine-tuning (task-specific distillation) stages.

components.name: General Distillation
components.function: Trains a general TinyBERT by having it mimic the original BERT (without fine-tuning) on a large-scale general-domain corpus using Transformer distillation, providing a good initialization.

components.name: Task-specific Distillation
components.function: Further fine-tunes the general TinyBERT on an augmented task-specific dataset, using a fine-tuned BERT as the teacher, to improve performance and generalization for downstream tasks.

components.name: Data Augmentation
components.function: Expands the task-specific training set by combining a pre-trained BERT and GloVe word embeddings to perform word-level replacement, enhancing the student model's generalization ability.

techniques.name: Attention based distillation
techniques.purpose: To transfer linguistic knowledge (syntax, coreference) captured by BERT's attention weights from teacher to student.
techniques.details: Student learns to fit the unnormalized attention matrices (A_i) of multi-head attention in the teacher network using Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss.

techniques.name: Hidden states based distillation
techniques.purpose: To distill knowledge from the output of Transformer layers.
techniques.details: Student learns to fit the hidden states (H) of the teacher network using MSE loss, incorporating a learnable linear transformation (W_h) to match hidden sizes.

techniques.name: Embedding-layer Distillation
techniques.purpose: To distill knowledge from the embedding layer.
techniques.details: Student learns to fit the embeddings (E) of the teacher network using MSE loss, with a linear transformation (W_e).

techniques.name: Prediction-layer Distillation
techniques.purpose: To fit the final predictions of the teacher model.
techniques.details: Uses soft cross-entropy (CE) loss between the student network's logits (z^S/t) and the teacher's logits (z^T/t), with a temperature value t=1.

techniques.name: Layer mapping function
techniques.purpose: To define which student layer learns from which teacher layer.
techniques.details: For TinyBERT_4, the mapping function is g(m) = 3 * m, meaning the m-th student layer learns from the (3*m)-th teacher layer.

techniques.name: Word-level replacement for data augmentation
techniques.purpose: To expand the task-specific training set and improve the student's generalization ability.
techniques.details: Uses BERT to predict word replacements for single-piece words and GloVe embeddings to retrieve similar words for multiple-piece words, with parameters p_t=0.4, N_a=20, K=15.

methodology.architecture: Transformer-based model; TinyBERT_4: 4 layers, hidden size d'=312, feed-forward size d'_f=1200, 12 attention heads; TinyBERT_6: 6 layers, hidden size d'=768, feed-forward size d'_f=3072, 12 attention heads.
methodology.model_size: TinyBERT_4: 14.5M parameters; TinyBERT_6: 67.0M parameters; BERT_BASE (Teacher): 109M parameters
methodology.training_objective: General Distillation: Intermediate layer distillation (embedding, hidden states, attention). Task-specific Distillation: Intermediate layer distillation followed by prediction layer distillation.
methodology.training_data: General Distillation: English Wikipedia (2,500M words). Task-specific Distillation: Augmented task-specific dataset.
methodology.compute_requirements: TinyBERT_4 inference speedup: 9.4x faster on a single NVIDIA K80 GPU compared to BERT_BASE.
methodology.inference_cost: TinyBERT_4 FLOPs: 1.2B; BERT_BASE FLOPs: 22.5B; TinyBERT_6 FLOPs: 11.3B.

datasets.name: QNLI
datasets.task: natural language inference (binary sentence pair classification)

settings: general distillation with max sequence length 128
task-specific distillation with max sequence length 64 for single-sentence tasks
task-specific distillation with max sequence length 128 for sequence pair tasks

contributions.description: Proposed a new Transformer distillation method to adequately transfer linguistic knowledge encoded in teacher BERT to TinyBERT.

Proposed a novel two-stage learning framework that performs Transformer distillation at both pre-training and fine-tuning stages, enabling TinyBERT to absorb both general-domain and task-specific knowledge from teacher BERT.

Demonstrated that TinyBERT_4 achieves more than 96.8% the performance of teacher BERT_BASE on GLUE tasks, with significantly fewer parameters (~13.3%) and less inference time (~10.6%), outperforming other 4-layer state-of-the-art baselines.
Showed that a 6-layer TinyBERT_6 can perform on-par with the teacher BERT_BASE on GLUE.

comparisons.difference: BERT_TINY is directly pre-trained as a small BERT, whereas TinyBERT uses a two-stage distillation framework to transfer knowledge from a larger teacher.
comparisons.evidence: TinyBERT_4 is consistently better than BERT_TINY on all GLUE tasks, with a 6.8% average improvement.

comparisons.difference: TinyBERT_4 employs a novel Transformer distillation method and a two-stage learning framework, while BERT-PKD extracts knowledge from intermediate layers at fine-tuning and DistilBERT performs distillation at the pre-training stage.
comparisons.evidence: TinyBERT_4 significantly outperforms these 4-layer state-of-the-art KD baselines by at least 4.4% on average.

comparisons.difference: BERT-PKD and DistilBERT initialize student models with layers from a pre-trained BERT, requiring the same Transformer layer size as the teacher. TinyBERT uses general distillation for initialization, allowing more flexible model configurations.
PD first pre-trains a small BERT and then distills it for a specific task. TinyBERT initializes the student for task-specific distillation via general distillation.
MobileBERT_TINY is a 24-layer model task-agnostically distilled from IB-BERT_LARGE, while TinyBERT_4 is a 4-layer model task-specifically distilled from BERT_BASE.
comparisons.evidence: TinyBERT_4 achieves the same average score (77.0) as the 24-layer MobileBERT_TINY with only 38.7% of its FLOPs.

limitations: All 4-layer distilled models, including TinyBERT_4, show big performance gaps compared to the teacher model on the challenging CoLA dataset.

The comparison between MobileBERT_TINY and TinyBERT_4 may not be entirely fair due to differences in layer count (24 vs 4) and teacher models (IB-BERT_LARGE vs BERT_BASE) and distillation scope (task-agnostic vs task-specific).
Adaptively choosing optimal layer mapping functions for specific tasks remains a challenging problem.
Question answering tasks, which depend on more subtle knowledge, increase the difficulty of knowledge distillation compared to sequence-level GLUE tasks.

Initializing TinyBERT without imitating BERT_BASE's behaviors at the pre-training stage (e.g., directly pre-training BERT_TINY) can lead to mismatched intermediate representations and poor performance on less-data tasks during subsequent task-specific distillation.
future_work: Study how to effectively transfer knowledge from wider and deeper teachers (e.g., BERT_LARGE) to student TinyBERT.
Combine distillation with quantization/pruning to further compress pre-trained language models.
Investigate adaptive layer mapping strategies for specific tasks.

key_terms.definition: A novel knowledge distillation method specially designed for Transformer-based models, involving fitting representations from embedding, Transformer, and prediction layers.
A framework for TinyBERT that performs Transformer distillation at both the pre-training (general distillation) and task-specific learning stages.
The first stage of TinyBERT learning where the original BERT (without fine-tuning) acts as the teacher, and TinyBERT mimics its behavior on a general-domain corpus.
The second stage of TinyBERT learning where a fine-tuned BERT acts as the teacher, and TinyBERT is distilled on an augmented task-specific dataset.
A component of Transformer distillation where the student learns to fit the unnormalized attention matrices of the teacher's multi-head attention layers using MSE loss.
A component of Transformer distillation where the student learns to fit the output hidden states of the teacher's Transformer layers using MSE loss, with a linear transformation.
A component of Transformer distillation where the student learns to fit the embeddings of the teacher network using MSE loss, with a linear transformation.
A component of Transformer distillation where the student learns to fit the predictions (logits) of the teacher model using soft cross-entropy loss.
A procedure used in task-specific distillation that combines BERT and GloVe word embeddings to perform word-level replacement, expanding the task-specific training set.
